value.toefl_ibt_scale_note: 89/22 applies to tests completed before January 21, 2026 (legacy 0-120 scale); for tests from January 21, 2026 the published minimum is on the new 1-6 scale

english.quote: The minimum requirement is an overall band of 6.5, with no band below 6.0.
english.how_found: future.utoronto.ca -> Apply -> English Language Requirements (direct URL; linked from the Computer Science programme page navigation as 'English Language Requirements').
english.notes: TOEFL iBT verbatim: 'The minimum requirement is an overall score of 4.5 with 4.5 in Writing and 4.0 in Speaking. For applicants who completed the test before January 21, 2026, the minimum requirement is a total score of 89 with 22 in each of Speaking and Writing.' Duolingo verbatim: 'The minimum requirement for tests completed on or after July 1st, 2024 is an overall score of 120 with a score of 120 in Production.' Who must prove English: 'If English is not your first language (i.e. is not the first language you learned at home as a child), you will need to provide evidence of adequate English facility for admission consideration, unless you qualify for an exemption.' IELTS and TOEFL scores must be achieved on a single date; TOEFL MyBest (super-scored) results are not used. A Kazakhstan NIS graduate whose first language is not English must present a test (or qualify for an exemption listed on the page).

value.description: No fixed minimum GPA, average or score is published for admission to the Computer Science admission category (Arts & Science, St. George). Admission is competitive: applicants meeting the minimum general and program-specific requirements are selected on competitive strength, with emphasis on the most recent two years of study. Kazakhstan minimum credential on the country list: 'Certificate of Completed Secondary Education' (no grade stated).

gpa.quote: The University of Toronto does not have the capacity to admit all applicants who meet the minimum general and program-specific requirements. We seek to admit the best possible students based on academic performance and potential, and will select students for admission based on competitive strength.
gpa.how_found: Computer Science programme page -> 'Assessment Process' link (how-your-application-considered). Country list found via search 'University of Toronto international students admission requirements Kazakhstan secondary school how your application is considered' -> https://future.utoronto.ca/high-school-requirements-country (Kazakhstan on ?page=3).
gpa.notes: Supporting quote from https://future.utoronto.ca/high-school-requirements-country: 'Please note that admission to the university is competitive and meeting minimum requirements does not guarantee admission.' Kazakhstan entry on https://future.utoronto.ca/high-school-requirements-country?page=3: 'Certificate of Completed Secondary Education' (no grade requirement listed). Also from the same assessment page: 'The emphasis of our final assessment will be placed on the results of your most recent two years of study.' Required courses for St. George CS: senior English (ENG4U/EAE4U equivalent) and Calculus & Vectors (MCV4U equivalent); a Computer Science Supplementary Application is required (programme page: 'Supplemental Application Required'). Note: once admitted to the CMP1 category, continuing into the CS Specialist/Major requires stated minimum grades in first-year CSC courses (calendar ASSPE1689: 'Students in the CMP1 admissions category have guaranteed admission to the Computer Science Specialist, provided the following courses with the stated minimum grades are successfully completed within 12 months').

tuition.quote: Admission Streams Year 1: Commerce, Computer Science, Humanities, Life Sciences, Mathematical and Physical Sciences, and Social Sciences | International Full-time Program Fee | Students with fewer than 4.0 credits completed | $66,110.00 | 2026/27 | Fall and Winter
tuition.how_found: future.utoronto.ca/finances/fees/ -> 'Current tuition fee schedules' (studentaccount.utoronto.ca, 301 -> www.registrar.utoronto.ca/tuition-fees/current-fall-winter-fee-refund-schedules/) -> 'Tuition Explorer' tool; the specific Explorer URL and the Planning & Budget PDF came from search 'University of Toronto tuition fee schedule 2026-27 international Arts & Science Computer Science planningandbudget'.
tuition.notes: Quote joins table cells with ' | '. 2027/28 fees are not yet approved; the latest approved and published year is 2026/27. Computer Science students pay the general Arts & Science first-year fee in Year 1 and a higher deregulated Computer Science fee from Year 2. Official PDF 'Tuition Fee Schedules for Publicly-Funded Programs 2026-27 March 1, 2026' (Planning & Budget Office), https://planningandbudget.utoronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2026-27-Tuition-Fee-Report_FINAL.pdf, p.23 (printed page 22), 'Table D2: International Tuition Fees for Undergraduate Programs with Higher Fees in Upper Years', columns '2025-26 | 2026-27 | 2027-28' headed 'APPROVAL | INFO'; verbatim rows: '2026 | Computer Science or Bioinformatics or Data Science | NA | $66,110 | $72,480' and '2027 | Computer Science or Bioinformatics or Data Science | NA | NA | $68,750'; table note: 'Students entering these programs pay a general Arts & Science program fee in Year 1.  They begin to pay a higher specialized program fee in Year 2 or Year 3'. PDF p.6: 'Fees for the upper years of these programs in 2027-28 will be submitted to Governing Council for approval in Spring 2027' and 'Commerce, Business Administration, and Management fees will increase by 4% while the other programs listed above will increase by 5% in 2026-27.' So a September 2027 entrant can expect roughly CAD 68,750 (info) in Year 1 (2027/28) and a higher CS fee (CAD 72,480 for 2027/28 per the 2026 cohort INFO column) from Year 2. Tuition Explorer note: 'UHIP is mandatory health insurance for all international students.'

value.name: Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarships

scholarship_exists.quote: Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarships
scholarship_exists.how_found: future.utoronto.ca/finances/scholarships/ -> link 'Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship' (/pearson-scholarships); URL confirmed by search 'Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship eligibility international students University of Toronto'. Page h1 verified from HTML.
scholarship_exists.notes: Coverage (page text): 'The Pearson International Student Scholarships cover tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years.' Requires school nomination: 'you need to be nominated by your school and apply to undergraduate studies at the University of Toronto'. Deadlines for September 2027 entry (verbatim): 'School nomination deadline: October 9, 2026'; 'Student OUAC admission application deadline: October 16, 2026'; 'Student scholarship application deadline and documentation submission deadline: November 6, 2026'. As of 2026-10-17 the nomination and OUAC deadlines have passed, so a new applicant can realistically only be considered if already nominated. Alternative with no separate application: 'University of Toronto Scholars Program' (https://future.utoronto.ca/university-of-toronto-scholars-program): 'There are approximately 900 admission awards, each of which has a value of $10,000.' and 'Outstanding domestic and international secondary school students are automatically considered'. General statement on https://future.utoronto.ca/finances/scholarships/: 'All admitted students, including international applicants, are automatically considered for admission scholarships.'

scholarship_international.quote: To be eligible to apply to the Pearson International Scholarship, you must be: an international student (i.e. a non-Canadian requiring a study permit);
scholarship_international.how_found: Same page as scholarship_exists ('BEFORE YOU APPLY - Confirm your eligibility' section); exact text verified from the page HTML.
scholarship_international.notes: Quote joins the lead-in sentence and the first bullet with a space. Further bullets: 'enrolled in your final year of senior secondary school in 2026/2027 or have graduated no earlier than June 2026; and' / 'beginning your studies at the University of Toronto in September 2027.' Also: 'Students who are already attending post-secondary studies or students who are starting their post-secondary studies in January 2027 at U of T or another post-secondary institution are not eligible'. A Kazakhstan citizen needing a study permit is within scope; the award is exclusively for international students.

The tool did save a copy of the PDF under its own tool-results folder as a side effect; it was not used.
The fetch tool's summaries cap quotes at ~125 characters; every quote used was re-verified verbatim against the page HTML via curl (future.utoronto.ca pages, Tuition Explorer).
No 2027/28 tuition schedule is approved yet; the only 2027-28 figures are 'INFO' columns in the 2026-27 report (recorded in tuition.value/notes, not as the main value).
